title: The Flea is always a lot of fun, but this year was pure chaos- let’s ...
transcript: I feel like we need to have a conversation about the Broadway Flea, because as much as I love it, and as much as I love the items that I got this year, I also feel like this year was kind of a shit show. I feel like every year it's gotten progressively more and more crowded, but this year especially, I felt like the crowds were truly problematic. Like, there were many, many times throughout the day where the sidewalk was just fully blocked with people and you could not get through. That's assuming you're just a pedestrian trying to get through. If you actually wanted to get to one of those tables, good luck. There were several tables this year that I just fully did not visit until the final hours of flea because the crowds around them were just too crazy. And I feel like in past years, they've handled this better. Like, I remember the Beetlejuice table last year was really popular, but they had a really long line. They would just wait in until you got to the front. Whereas this year was just kind of a free for all at all of the popular tables. And if you're not pushing your way to the front, you probably weren't getting to the front. And so not only were the crowds really overwhelming, but I felt like it also encouraged people to be aggressive and to push people out of the way, which is just never Fun for anyone. I've been going to the flea pretty consistently since 2015, and I feel like when I first started going, the tables were flipped the other way towards the street. So if you wanted to browse the tables, you would walk down the street, and then the sidewalks were cleared for pedestrians. And I feel like this setup just works so much better, because 1, there's just more room in the streets for people, and 2, on the sidewalks, you still have people trying to rush Broadway shows, you have people trying to get in line for their Sunday matinees. But I think that keeping that walkway open is just really important. And what's weird is they ended up blocking off the roads anyway, so you would have these big crowds of people, but then you would look behind the tables and there was just this big empty space. And it felt like we could have been using that. And so in future years, I hope they go back to that previous setup, cause I really do think that it did wonders in terms of crowd control. And given that it's gotten crazier and crazier every year, if this is how crazy it was this year, I'm really nervous for the crowds next year.
